original_problem: Graham1971Question12 literally asks completeness for positive alpha,beta with irrational ratio at base2 and then what if2 is replaced by some1<gamma<2. Exponents start0; sequences not deduplicated. Fresh original page visually read by root.
scope_correction: Do not exclude a complete counterexample to the universal variable-base clause merely because base2 or a full base classification remains open. Eligibility provisional; no scientific publication approved.
root_proof_read: Full9813-byte PROOF and scopeJSON/README/PR; root manually checked quartic root/coefficient bounds, trace recurrence, strict all-future shift20 and irrational ratio.
primary_priority_read: Fresh Glasgow2006p332Theorem1(iv)/exactquartic family and p334proof; Archivum2006p154Theorem4/positive c and p156proof. Full source bytes retained, not a claim to independent proof audits of every result in either paper.
root_priority_deduction: The older published positive multiplier c=1/((gamma-1)Pprime(gamma)) has fractional parts tending to1/3 for this irreducible Pisot quartic withP(1)=-3. ChooseN so all later fractional parts lie strictly between0 and1/2. WithA=2c*gamma^N andB=gamma*A, all indexed floor terms in both sequences are even, A/B=1/gamma irrational, so every odd integer is missing. Thus the full negative universal variable-base answer follows directly from old theory; PR's explicitN20 is a quantitative realization, not required for that full conclusion.
priority_boundary: Root does not claim that Dubickas names Graham's question, that no earlier/later literal application exists, or that all good/bad bases have been classified. Independent adversary may challenge scope or the old-theory deduction before disposition.
